title: 20 AI Fundraising Stories Worth Studying Before You Build a Deck
summary: 20 AI Fundraising Stories Worth Studying Before You Build a Deck
body_markdown:
An AI demo can be impressive and still tell you very little about the company. If a founder chooses the prompt, cleans the input, and keeps the errors offscreen, the audience learns what happened once. The harder question is what happens on Tuesday when a customer does it without you.


Here are 20 public financing stories and investment notes worth reading with that question in mind. Most are written by companies or their investors. They are not private pitch decks, independent audits, or proof that a particular slide caused a round. What they give you is a useful way to think about the evidence your own deck needs.


## Show the repeatable work


- [Cursor](https://a16z.com/announcement/investing-in-cursor/) : Make it clear where the AI appears in the working environment. What does a developer finish faster after a week?
- [Zed](https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-zed-the-ai-powered-code-editor-built-from-scratch) : Show how the interface and collaboration model fit the workflow. Who returns to the editor once novelty wears off?
- [Harvey](https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-harvey-putting-llms-to-work) : Define a professional task and who verifies the result. How long does a lawyer spend checking the output?
- [Vals](https://a16z.com/announcement/investing-in-vals/) : Make evaluation part of the product story, not a footnote. How is a bad answer detected on real work?
- [Hebbia](https://a16z.com/announcement/investing-in-hebbia/) : Name the source set and what a user produces from it. Can a reviewer trace the result to a source?
- [Glean](https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-glean-organizing-knowledge-work) : Explain the cost of finding a known answer across tools. Do employees return after installing it?


## Show the result and the handoff


- [Exa](https://a16z.com/announcement/investing-in-exa/) : Show why the retrieval problem changes for a machine client. What does the generated answer gain from better sources?
- [Decagon](https://a16z.com/announcement/investing-in-decagon/) : Define when the system can resolve an issue and when it hands off. What share of resolutions stay resolved?
- [Fyxer](https://landing.fyxer.com/blog/series-b-statement) : Pair speed of growth with a measure of repeated use. Does a user hand it more inbox work over time?
- [Profound](https://www.tryprofound.com/blog/series-a) : Give the buyer a new observation they can act on. Which observation leads to an action someone repeats?
- [ElevenLabs](https://a16z.com/announcement/investing-in-elevenlabs/) : Connect output quality to a production task and constraints. How often does a producer ship the first usable result?
- [Sesame](https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-sesame-a-new-era-for-voice) : Separate a convincing demonstration from regular reliance. How many listeners start a second conversation?


## Show where the demo breaks


- [Decart](https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-decart-the-future-of-ai-generated-experiences) : For interactive products, put latency and continuity on the same chart. What changes when the user interrupts?
- [Preview](https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-preview-lights-inference-action) : Make the inference work behind a creative workflow visible. What does a finished, accepted output cost?
- [Bunkerhill Health](https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-bunkerhill-health-ai-agents-that-improve-patient-outcomes) : Say how the product fits existing human oversight. Who checks a missed or incorrect action, and when?
- [Slingshot AI](https://a16z.com/announcement/investing-in-slingshot-ai/) : Explain how you test limits in a sensitive domain. Which scenarios require a different path or escalation?


## Show the cost and the failure mode


- [Etched](https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-etched-building-the-inference-machine) : Name the trade-off of specialization. Under what workload does the performance comparison hold?
- [Nexthop AI](https://a16z.com/announcement/investing-in-nexthop/) : Tie infrastructure to a specific scale or operating constraint. Which customer cost changes after deployment?
- [Air](https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-air-securing-the-ai-supply-chain) : Identify the risk boundary before describing the coverage. Who owns a failed test, and what action do they take?
- [Temporal](https://a16z.com/announcement/investing-in-temporal/) : Show what happens when a long-running workflow fails halfway through. Can a real run recover without duplicating work?


## Choose the evidence that can fail


A strong metric can move in the wrong direction. Time to a checked result can get longer. More customers can stop using a feature. Those are useful numbers because they tell you what to fix. “Touches AI” and “total prompts” may go up no matter how much work still falls to the customer.


Take three of the examples above and turn them into one test for your business. Write down the result you expect, the comparison, and what you would do if you were wrong. Suppose you draft a first pass at a financial report. Compare the time to a reviewer-approved report this month with the time for the same kind of report last month, using similar accounts. Keep your exceptions. The before-and-after chart will be useful only if you can tell someone what the work looked like on both sides.


Put the cleanest result in the deck and the original evidence nearby. The first makes the point. The second lets someone check it.
